source.title: FlippedRAG: Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Adversarial Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models

idea.title: Transferable Poisoning Technique for Influencing Knowledge-Enhanced Language Models on Controversial Topics
idea.purpose: Current security evaluations of knowledge-enhanced language frameworks lack realistic threat models capable of shifting viewpoints on complex subjects under opaque access conditions.
idea.mechanism: The approach reverse-engineers the underlying document lookup component through query enumeration to train a local proxy, which is then used to craft subtle document poisonings that alter both the lookup and synthesis phases for successful transfer to the target system.
idea.evaluation: Extensive empirical results show that the technique substantially outperforms baseline methods, improving the average attack success rate by 16.7% and achieving a 50% directional shift in generated opinion polarity across four diverse domains.

idea.title: Optimizing Multi-Component Knowledge-Enhanced Language Generation via Cooperative Reinforcement Learning
idea.purpose: Current knowledge-augmented text generation pipelines optimize their modular components independently, leading to misaligned objectives and suboptimal final answer accuracy.
idea.mechanism: The framework models each pipeline stage as a cooperative reinforcement learning agent, harmonizing all module goals toward a unified final answer reward.
idea.evaluation: It is tested on various question-answering benchmarks by comparing performance against existing baselines and conducting comprehensive ablation studies.

idea.title: Enhancing Text Search and Answering via Inverted Query Indexing Strategies
idea.purpose: This work addresses the information dilution and hallucination challenges faced by conventional search-augmented text generation systems when handling vast amounts of data.
idea.mechanism: The approach generates potential inquiries from document segments and matches these directly against user search terms to identify the most relevant context blocks for formulating accurate responses.
idea.evaluation: The system is evaluated against traditional search-augmented pipelines using BERT-Score and text generation assessment metrics on a custom corpus with manually prepared ground truth data.

source.title: SaLoRA: Safety-Alignment Preserved Low-Rank Adaptation

idea.title: Preserving Safety Alignment During Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
idea.purpose: This work addresses the problem of parameter-efficient adaptation techniques inadvertently compromising the safety alignment of large language models during personalization.
idea.mechanism: The approach analyzes safety alignment features before and after adaptation, then introduces a fixed safety module derived from safety data combined with a task-specific initialization for trainable parameters. This design enables targeted task modifications while preventing disruption to the model's original safety behaviors.
idea.evaluation: Experiments are conducted to evaluate performance against various adapter-based approaches across multiple metrics and fine-tuning tasks.

source.title: TriAdaptLoRA: Brain-Inspired Triangular Adaptive Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

idea.title: Dynamic Triangular Decomposition and Growth for Efficient Language Model Customization
idea.purpose: This work addresses the high computational costs of fully adjusting large language models while overcoming the limited flexibility of existing parameter-reduction techniques.
idea.mechanism: It splits transformation matrices into lower and upper components, measures parameter importance using normalized Frobenius norms, and dynamically grows the matrix ranks via threshold-driven strategies during training.
idea.evaluation: Experiments across multiple natural language understanding and generation tasks demonstrate that this framework surpasses baseline approaches in performance, stability, and computational overhead.

idea.title: Dynamic Structure Optimization for Efficient Modular Adaptation in Large Language Models
idea.purpose: This work addresses parameter redundancy, rigid design, and limited task adaptability when updating massive neural networks.
idea.mechanism: It employs differentiable gating functions and sparsity controls to automatically optimize insertion locations, activation paths, and module combinations while keeping the backbone frozen. A structure search mechanism dynamically constructs task-specific efficient substructures during training to enhance capacity.
idea.evaluation: It is tested across multiple natural language understanding tasks to measure accuracy, compression rate, and robustness against mainstream tuning baselines.

idea.title: External Knowledge Integration for Scientific Synthesis in Materials Science
idea.purpose: Existing tools extract narrow, study-specific facts in isolation and fail to preserve the cross-study context needed for systematic scientific reasoning over unstructured texts.
idea.mechanism: We construct context-preserving paragraph embeddings using dense semantic vectors alongside a canonicalized structured knowledge graph that supports entity disambiguation and multi-hop reasoning.

idea.title: Dynamic Parameter Consolidation for Extended Sequence Processing Tasks
idea.purpose: Transformers struggle with expansive sequences because uniform test-time parameter updates waste compute on uninformative regions and exhibit high gradient variance.
idea.mechanism: A specialized write controller assesses information-theoretic long-range dependence to selectively gate gradient update steps while maintaining global sequence coverage. This approach allocates computational budgets dynamically based on estimated utility rather than updating continuously.
idea.evaluation: Experiments on ZeroSCROLLS and LongBench v2 demonstrate that the approach achieves comparable or superior performance with four times fewer gradient steps than uniform baselines.

idea.title: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Assessing Extended Audio Dialogue Comprehension
idea.purpose: Current audio models struggle to retain salient information across extended audio inputs, which act as a low-compression modality requiring many embeddings.
idea.mechanism: The framework systematically extends audio history along turn count and duration dimensions across diverse scenarios, providing explicit answer-provenance annotations and length-aware organization.
idea.evaluation: Extensive evaluations of seven representative spoken language models are conducted to reveal overall recency effects and retrieval limitations across varying dialogue lengths.

idea.title: Assessing Extended Span Source Attribution Capabilities in Large Language Models
idea.purpose: This work addresses the underexplored ability of extended-span language models to attribute items of interest to specific parts of extensive text data.
idea.mechanism: The proposed evaluation framework requires models to identify the indexes of documents referencing a specific key by emphasizing contextual relationships rather than simple retrieval across three constructed subsets ranging from synthetic to realistic scenarios.
idea.evaluation: Thirteen advanced language models are tested on the benchmark, revealing significant shortcomings that are further investigated through human evaluations, format adjustments, fine-tuning, and error analyses.

idea.title: Bridging Offline Pretraining and Online Fine-Tuning via Adaptive Behavior Consistency
idea.purpose: This work addresses the poor performance and unstable value estimates of policies transitioned from static datasets to dynamic online environments.
idea.mechanism: The framework utilizes an implicit behavioral model from offline data to impose a consistency constraint during online fine-tuning, dynamically relaxing this restriction as uncertainty decreases and confidence grows.
idea.evaluation: It is tested on standard environments to demonstrate faster recovery, increased robustness, and superior overall performance compared to prior techniques.

source.title: Offline RL with Smooth OOD Generalization in Convex Hull and its Neighborhood

idea.title: Enhancing Offline Reinforcement Learning via Smooth Bellman Operators in Convex Hull Neighborhoods
idea.purpose: This work addresses the problem of over-conservatism and Q-value overestimation in offline reinforcement learning when handling out-of-distribution actions.
idea.mechanism: A smooth Bellman operator updates out-of-distribution Q-values by smoothing them with neighboring in-sample values within the convex hull and its neighborhood, ensuring safe generalization guarantees.
idea.evaluation: It is tested on standard robotic manipulation and navigation benchmarks to demonstrate superior performance and computational efficiency compared to existing baselines.

idea.title: Learning Latency-Resilient Control Policies from Static Datasets Using Transformer Belief Predictors
idea.purpose: This work addresses the challenge of deploying static-trained control agents into dynamic environments that introduce execution latency, which violates the Markov assumption and causes performance degradation.
idea.mechanism: The framework utilizes a transformer-based belief predictor to generate latency-resilient actions during online deployment, despite being trained exclusively on latency-free logs.
idea.evaluation: It is tested on standard simulation benchmarks across multiple latency configurations, comparing performance against history-augmentation and alternative prediction baselines.

source.title: Do Counterfactually Fair Image Classifiers Satisfy Group Fairness? - A Theoretical and Empirical Study

idea.title: Investigating Counterfactual and Group Fairness Relationships in Image Classification
idea.purpose: The unclear relationship between counterfactual fairness and group fairness in image classification tasks due to the lack of suitable image datasets.
idea.mechanism: By constructing new image datasets using high-quality image editing and human annotations based on popular group fairness benchmarks, we empirically and theoretically analyze how latent attributes correlated with sensitive features affect both fairness notions and propose a distillation approach to mitigate this reliance.
idea.evaluation: Extensive experimental results on the newly constructed image datasets demonstrate that counterfactual-fair models satisfy group fairness when reliance on the correlated latent attribute is successfully reduced.

idea.title: Analyzing the Effects of Duplicate Images on Standard and Robust Image Classifiers
idea.purpose: This study addresses the lack of understanding regarding how duplicated images in training sets affect the generalization and performance of deep neural network image classifiers.
idea.mechanism: We comprehensively analyze how uniform and non-uniform image duplication across classes impacts training efficiency and accuracy for both standard and adversarially trained models.
idea.evaluation: The study is evaluated by empirically analyzing model training efficiency and accuracy under various image duplication conditions in the training sets.

idea.title: Overcoming Spurious Correlations via Counterfactual Generation and Knowledge Distillation
idea.purpose: This work addresses the vulnerability of deep learning classifiers to spurious correlations and Clever Hans predictors when group labels are unavailable or sample sizes are small.
idea.mechanism: The framework generates diverse counterfactuals to enrich undersampled groups and allows efficient correction of decision boundaries through a knowledge distillation step without requiring confounder labels.
idea.evaluation: The efficacy of the approach is demonstrated across five datasets spanning synthetic tasks to industrial applications, supplemented by ablation studies on counterfactual explainers and teacher models.

idea.title: A Benchmark for Assessing Automated Critiques in MultiStep Agentic Systems
idea.purpose: Evaluating agent trajectories at scale currently relies on automated judges whose critiques often lack measured soundness due to the high cost of human annotation.
idea.mechanism: Human annotators evaluate openweight judge critiques on agent tasks by labeling flagged errors for location accuracy and reasoning quality, achieving strong inter-annotator agreement.
idea.evaluation: It compares openweight judge models across varying capability levels and reasoning efforts to measure their human agreement rates on error location and reasoning.

source.title: BayesJudge: Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian Meta-Evaluation of Human and LLM Judgments

idea.title: Probabilistic Online Layer for Resolving Conflicting Evaluation Streams
idea.purpose: This work addresses the problem of conflicting decisions in AI assessment pipelines caused by ambiguous items, unstable annotators, and model order biases.
idea.mechanism: The system estimates a posterior distribution over response comparisons using an online Bayesian recursion while simultaneously calculating annotator confusion matrices and model position biases. It leverages tie-open labels to preserve ambiguity and employs paired order-swapped queries to decouple quality from presentation effects via a scalable sequential Monte Carlo approximation.
idea.evaluation: The approach is tested through controlled synthetic experiments to recover evaluator parameters and on a real-world summarization benchmark to detect order biases, infer behavioral signatures, and correlate uncertainty with annotator disagreement.

source.title: LLM-as-a-Judge: Rapid Evaluation of Legal Document Recommendation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

idea.title: Automating Legal Retrieval Evaluation Using Generative Models as Judges
idea.purpose: This paper addresses the evaluation bottleneck in specialized legal recommendation systems by investigating whether large language models can reliably serve as automated judges.
idea.mechanism: We examine various inter-rater reliability metrics and statistical tests to determine alignment between model and human assessments, finding that specific agreement coefficients and rank correlations combined with corrected significance tests offer a robust framework.
idea.evaluation: Through systematic experimentation on skewed distribution data, we evaluate different agreement metrics and statistical comparison techniques to establish a rigorous, scalable evaluation methodology.
